answer: Cross-epoch behaviour matching. Each identity commits a hidden behavioural digest per epoch; the next epoch’s actions must reproduce it within tolerance. An agent whose fable of past activity diverges pays a continuity deposit forfeited on mismatch. Sybils must maintain consistent histories across every epoch, so each fake identity costs sustained compute plus a forfeitable deposit, and any whisper of inconsistency triggers slashing. A raven flag marks identities that fail twice, blocking re-entry.
